turn_text: Thank you for allowing us to visit with you today and I look forward to it.

Congressman Sutherland, you are a conferee on the farm food and jobs bill. When do you think these three initial bills, one from the Senate and two from the House, will be resolved to the point they can be passed back to both Houses of Congress?

Well, we're optimistic that we will have a farm bill done by the end of the year. I know that last week we were in our districts and the day before we left, we had our opening conference meeting. which I'm sure your listeners were aware of. And so we're hitting the ground running today is our first day back. And so we believe as the leaders have conveyed that there is time and there is a desire to get a farm bill done and hopefully by your end.
Your amendment was credited with breaking the back of democratic support of that original House Farm Bill. How did that really play out?

Well, I think I learned a valuable lesson here that even in a bill that is so critical to try to create certainty for the people that the bill affects, in this town, politics plays in to the equation. I was deeply disappointed by the accusation that my bill was meant. to take down the farm bill because that could be nothing farther from the truth. I have several pieces of legislative efforts that are inside the farm bill and my belief, deeply held belief regarding food stamps is that able-bodied individuals who are of working age, who are mentally, physically, psychologically able to work should either work, train for work, look for work, or even volunteer in their local communities. And so to take our honest intentions to introduce the blessing of work to some four to five million recipients of food stamps and to turn that and to twist that into something other than my honest intentions, I think was extremely disappointing. It was something we've been working on for well over a year. So there was no secret what we were doing and there was no secret the motives that we have which were totally pure to make sure that those that are physically able to work would work. I was kind of amazed at the backlash from the other side of the aisle but it is no secret that I am one of the top 10 targets of the Democratic Congressional Committee going into the next election cycle next fall, and unfortunately I think that the fact that I am in a race that is going to be very watched by both sides of the aisle, unfortunately that played in to some, and I think that is extremely unfortunate.
